quote:
She asked if she could buy anything for the baby. I told her “yeah, sure. Something simple. My mom is going to make a blanket… I think a body or a swaddle blanket is okay. We decided we’ll buy the baby stuff by the end of the year” Then she herself told me “of course, I thought of something simple, like a burp cloth”, then I said “yes!!! This would be amazing!”

Then there was this and everything else lol
cx: First trimester; her in-laws then arrived with a suitcase of baby things, nearly a full hospital bag.

quote: Yeah, a bunch of stuff they bought is very practical and can be easily forgotten. That’s why I am grateful and confused… I don’t want to come across ungrateful or petty.
cx: Same mother, replying to commenters about the in-laws' haul.

quote: they say something along the lines of “you’re getting close!!!! How are you feeling?” And “would love to see a pic of your bump!” 1. I know im getting close🙂 I’m hot, uncomfortable, and swollen. This hasn’t changed for the past couple weeks.
cx: 36 weeks, first baby; three of her husband's relatives text daily.

quote: We’ve already agreed that we’ll be waiting a couple days prior to letting anyone on his side of the family know when our son is born - they all talk, so if we were to tell one person, they’d all know. We’re also not taking any visitors immediately when we come home from the hospital […] My mom is going to come once we’ve been home for a week or two depending on how we’re feeling.
cx: The couple's plan for announcing and visitors.

quote: We’re still trying to finish up the nursery and both still working full time. Fortunately, we both get generous amounts paid maternity/paternity leave, so there’s a light at the end of the tunnel
This is a lesson I don’t think I’ll ever forget - be overly selective about the info we share throughout pregnancy😅

A lot of the conversation around newborns focuses on the mother, ie postpartum recovery, breastfeeding, hormones, etc. and all of that is completely valid and important. But it can also feel like the expectation is that dads just power through and aren’t really allowed to be tired or struggle.
cx: A father outside the US with an 8-week-old, worn out.

quote: When I got pregnant, my husband and I specifically asked everyone to keep it private because we weren't ready to tell people yet. She completely ignored that and told friends and family anyway
cx: A mother of two on her sister-in-law.

quote: she just started covering her own ears while looking at us like we were retards. She continued doing it for about ten minutes, and the whole thing felt like she was trying to prove a point. Then she turned to my husband and said, "This is how you do it."
cx: At fireworks, while the couple covered their baby's ears.

quote: Now I'm pregnant with our fourth baby—our first girl after three boys. We recently had a 3D ultrasound, and she posted one of the ultrasound pictures along with a collage of me, my fiancé, and our three kids on Facebook. She never asked if she could post it.
cx: Her mother-in-law also posted the third baby's birth announcement first.

quote: When we told her the baby is due in January, she immediately started making comments about how we "didn't plan right."
cx: The mother-in-law's reply to the due date.

quote: my fiancé and I have already agreed that neither of his parents will be allowed to bring their phones into the hospital when the baby is born. Last time, they stayed for maybe five minutes, took pictures, and left. It felt like they came for a photo opportunity instead of to meet their grandchild.
cx: Her hospital rule for the fourth birth, based on the third.

quote: However over thing I keep reading here and other parent forums, is the constant tiredness and exhaustion. […] some people write they didn't get a good night sleep the first 4 years, and that sounds like an actual nightmare to me
cx: A first-time father at seven weeks, after reading parent forums.

quote: She of course wants to come a stay with us for about 4 days over Thanksgiving break and again for longer over Christmas break. I know i wont feel up to hosting at Thanksgiving. I probably still wont at Christmas.. but we could maybe cover the cost of a hotel at christmas time so she has somewhere to go so I can rest in my own home and not be confined to pumping in my bedroom while she's here.
cx: Due 12 days before Thanksgiving with her third; her mother-in-law teaches five hours away.

quote: the truth is she is zero help when she's here.. my mom and sister are already making plans to come and cook and clean and care for my older 2 so I get a break. They aren't just coming by to hold the baby for days on end. Its a completely different situation.
cx: Helpers versus visitors after her third birth.

quote: As my due date approaches, my husband finds out he has to take a nonnegotiable work trip when I am 3 weeks PP. as I’m telling my friend about this (she would be helping me out while my husband is gone), she tells me that her new boyfriend (1 month at the time) really wants to visit the major city in my state (4 hours away from my town) and will be coming along with her.
cx: Her best friend lives across the country and had offered to stay and help.

quote: From what I’ve seen, it’ll be close to 1000$ just for the expenses when they get here (rental car, hotel, gas, etc) and that just seems extreme
cx: The cost of a friend's helping visit shrunk to two days.

quote: he has made multiple comments about pregnancy related things that I’ve told her about (birth plan, diet, name choice) and he just comes off as a know it all
cx: Her friend's new boyfriend, who has never spoken to her.
